extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, education theorists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and criteria for organizing school curricula and pedagogical practice to integrate natural sciences and humanistic studies, foster social-minded inquiry, and prepare citizens in a democratic society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-fertilize natural sciences and human disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should take its departure from the close interdependence of humanistic and naturalistic studies and aim at cross-fertilizing the natural sciences and the various human disciplines such as history, literature, economics, and politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not keep science as a study of nature apart from literature as a record of human interests. Arrange curriculum and instruction so that scientific study is connected with social, historical, economic, and literary contexts; promote interdisciplinary projects and examples showing relations among fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid segregated, technically organized subject-matter at the start
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning instruction with technically organized subject matter (the specialized bodies of prior specialization) institutes an artificial separation in pupils' experience and makes sciences appear unrelated to human affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: introducing college/high-school students to segregated scientific subjects as if they were intended only for specialists. Instead, start from experience and practical contexts rather than abstract technical presentation; avoid smoothing difficulties merely to create an elementary version of specialist material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize ordinary experience to introduce scientific method
rubrics_metrics.description: The obvious pedagogical starting point of scientific instruction is not to teach things labeled 'science' but to utilize the familiar occupations and appliances to direct observation and experiment until pupils arrive at fundamental principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common technologies (steam engines, automobiles, telegraph, electric motor, household pursuits, public sanitation) and students' lived experiences as entry points for directed observation and experiment. Build from practical phenomena toward underlying principles and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach scientific facts in their social and human context
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception of meanings depends upon perception of connections and context; to see a scientific fact or law in its human as well as its physical and technical context enlarges its cultural value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the function of scientific knowledge in life and social uses rather than only its technical or economic applications. Encourage students to consider social, moral, and aesthetic implications of scientific discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve qualitative aspects and values in science education
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject philosophies of science that reduce all qualities to subjective impressions and treat objective existence as only quantitative; qualities (sounds, colors, goods, bads) are part of reality and relevant to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not teach science solely as prediction and control of events stripped of qualities. Incorporate discussions of qualitative experience, values, and meanings alongside technical instruction to avoid a barren, monotonous view of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanistic studies must cultivate concern for social well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanism means an intelligent sense of human interests; humanistic study should increase concern for values of life and produce greater sensitiveness to social well-being, not merely accumulate technical facts about literature or history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess humanistic learning by its ability to enlarge imaginative vision and promote social concern. Anti-pattern: studies that become 'a miser's accumulation' of facts without enlarging meaning or moral imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand humanism to include economic and industrial conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Older humanism omitted economic and industrial conditions and became one-sided; a democratic education must take greater account of industry and making-a-living so culture is not merely aristocratic preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceive industrial activities as agencies for making intellectual resources accessible to the masses. Integrate study of economic and industrial realities into cultural education to broaden its social relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide opportunity for scientific specialization without isolating general students
rubrics_metrics.description: While education should provide chances for those disposed to advance to specialized ability in science, the majority who study science for habits of mind should not be confined to superficial or purely technical presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance pathways: maintain specialized tracks for budding scientists while ensuring general education uses scientific method and applications relevantly for all pupils. Avoid producing a 'smattering' that is too superficial to be scientific and too technical to be applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster individual reconstruction of beliefs via inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of the individual in knowledge is the redirection or reconstruction of accepted beliefs; every new idea must originate in an individual and be pursued, tested, and elaborated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to observe, form hypotheses, and test them; value personal initiative in generating new ideas. Support experimental and inductive approaches as legitimate means for discovery and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the social nature of mind and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Mind is not a purely isolated possession of the self; the self achieves mind through a social medium—social intercourse and shared activities are the means by which individuals acquire knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning as social and collaborative: use shared activities, discussion, mutual testing of hypotheses, and collective inquiry. Avoid pedagogies that treat interest and knowledge as purely private matters detached from community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish settled knowledge from active thinking and promote both appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is what is taken for granted and enables unhesitating action; thinking starts from doubt and inquiry and serves to revise and extend settled knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students both to rely on established knowledge where appropriate and to cultivate habits of inquiry and critical thinking that can reorganize beliefs. Emphasize when to accept settled practice and when to investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject excessive deference to authority in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that set apart sacred domains of truth and emphasize authority of book and teacher discourage individual variation and intellectual responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid curricula and classroom practices that present truths as unchallengeable. Instead, cultivate critical examination of received beliefs and encourage testing and verification by pupils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on abstract rationalism detached from subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal intellectualism or rationalism that treats reason as a faculty apart from concrete subject matter is useful in criticism but impotent in constructing new subject matter or specific aims and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on abstract rules; connect reasoning to historical institutions, habits, emotions, and concrete contexts. Ensure logical instruction is grounded in substantive materials and practical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reduce civic education to mere self-interest via commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Appealing only to intelligent self-interest (trade-based harmony) to secure social unity is limited; education should instill regard for others, not merely non-interference or profit-driven cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance civic and moral education so pupils learn obligations beyond market transactions. Use civic examples and moral reasoning to foster positive regard for others, not just legal or economic incentives.
